name: itpp
desc: Library of math, signal, and communication classes and functions
why: IT++ communications and signal processing library, a real door into channel coding and DSP, though mostly a C++ library.

brief.what_it_is: IT++ is a C++ library of mathematical, signal processing and communication classes and functions, according to its SourceForge description. Its main use is simulating communication systems and doing communications research. You link it into your own C++ code, so the inputs and outputs are program data rather than a standalone tool. The SourceForge page lists BSD, Cygwin, Linux, Mac, MinGW/MSYS2 and Solaris as operating systems. The Homebrew formula installs an executable named itpp-config.
brief.why_it_exists: Its main use is in simulation of communication systems and for performing research in the area of communications.
brief.install_notes: I saw no install steps beyond the Homebrew formula, which installs an executable named itpp-config. The homepage and SourceForge page gave no build, dependency or configuration instructions, and I did not read a README or docs that covered them.
brief.standout: Its niche is a C++ toolkit aimed at communications research, and the scout note points to channel coding and DSP as the real draw. One SourceForge reviewer says a bit matrix and Hadamard transform were not available in any other C++ library, and another says Armadillo is faster for matrix operations with more functionality.
brief.status: quiet. The SourceForge page shows a last update of 2018-05-29, a registration date of 2001-10-04, and 53 downloads this week at the time of the crawl. I could not confirm current activity, and I found no release or commit information.
brief.caveats: The homepage is only a stub that redirects to SourceForge, so I worked from the SourceForge project page and never read a README or docs. A guessed GitHub URL returned 404. The SourceForge page is reviews plus metadata, not the project's own documentation. The reviewer comparison with Armadillo is one user's opinion. The license is GPLv2, which matters for anyone embedding it in closed code.
